blocks.text: B2-13 · Translation from Arabic: method
Lesson overview

With the module B2.3 translation becomes the center of work. So far you have translated sentences to verify understanding; now learn to produce a professional translation: faithful in content, natural in English, verifiable. An Arabic journalistic text translated word by word gives a heavy and sometimes wrong Italian: very long sentences linked by In this unit you learn a method in four phases (understand, disassemble, reformulate, revise) and the most frequent transformations between Arabic and Italian: from maṣdar to the verb, from the chain of ⁧و⁩ to Italian periods, from ḥāl to the gerund, from the passive with ⁧تَمَّ⁩ Italian forms, repetitions to synonyms and pronouns. A new teacher leads you, the professor. Ṭāhā ʿAbd al-ḤamīdEgyptian translator. Four weeks, in parallel with the start of EGY-17.

rows: Modules B2.1 and B2.2; B2-02 (long-term syntax)
20–22 hours · four weeks (weeks 208–211), plus the EGY track in separate blocks

blocks.text: Materials This unit, Reference Grammar (G)72), dictionary by root, a monolingual Italian dictionary, sessions with the tutor
Targets. At the end of the lesson you know:
1. to apply to a text of 200 words a four-step translation method;
2. divide a long Arabic period into natural Italian periods, preserving logical relationships;
3. apply frequent transformations (maṣdar → verb, ḥāl → gerund or relative, ⁧تَمَّ⁩ + maṣdar → passive, repetition → pronoun or synonym);
4. treat own names, titles, dates, numbers and quotations according to Italian conventions;
5. review a translation with a checklist and evaluate it with the Accuracy / Return section.
Four-week plan.

2. The four phases

blocks.text: The phase 4 It's done twice. The first revision compares with Arabic (Accuracy); the second forgets Arabic and reads Italian as a reader who does not know it (Resa). If a sentence sounds strange, the reader will not understand it.
3. Disassemble period
The Arab journalistic period is often a chain: main sentence + ⁧و⁩ + ⁧و⁩ + ḥāl + relative + ⁧فِيمَا⁩ …. Italian prefers shorter periods, with explicit connections. Example.
⁧وَأَعْلَنَتِ الوِزَارَةُ عَنْ خُطَّةٍ لِتَحْدِيثِ شَبَكَةِ القِطَارَاتِ، تَبْلُغُ كُلْفَتُهَا مِلْيَارَيْ دُولَارٍ، وَتَمْتَدُّ عَلَى خَمْسِ سَنَوَاتٍ،⁩
⁧مُؤَكِّدَةً أَنَّ الأَشْغَالَ سَتَبْدَأُ فِي الرَّبِيعِ، فِيمَا شَكَّكَتِ النِّقَابَاتُ فِي إِمْكَانِيَّةِ احْتِرَامِ الجَدْوَلِ الزَّمَنِيِّ.⁩

Checklist (to be used for each translation).

rows: Did I translate everything? No sentences, no skippings?
Numbers, dates, names, numbers: one by one against the original
Attribution verbs and preserved degrees of certainty (B2-08, B2-09)?
Denials ( ⁧لَمْ⁩ , ⁧لَنْ⁩ , ⁧لَا⁩ , ⁧غَيْرُ⁩ ) and double negations made correctly?
Connotations and metaphors made with the same weight (B2-11)?
Periods in Italy of reasonable length, with clear connections?
No casts (the agreement has taken place)?
Repetitions handled with pronouns or synonyms?
Final reading aloud, without looking at Arabic

blocks.text: The address book (over the entire form). Accuracy 1–4: 4 = complete and precise; 3 = an inaccurate detail that does not change the meaning; 2 = an error that changes a part of the meaning (a digit, a negation, a degree of certainty); 1 = compromised sense. Yield 1–4: 4 = natural Italian, as an original article; 3 = some heavy cast or phrase; 2 = Italian tiring, more casts; 1 = you can understand only by reading Arabic.
